Include a large generated board preview as the focal area, a structured rule editor panel, controls for board size and initial layout, a few rule toggles or parameter fields, a compact validation summary, and prominent Generate Board and Start Game actions. Put strong emphasis on making complex configuration approachable through hierarchy, grouping, feedback, and a polished tabletop-tool identity.

history.critique: Brief & Intent: The two required primary actions — Generate Board and Start Game — are absent from the visible screen; the only action is a quiet 'EXPORT .TSM' in the header, so the core 'forge' moment is missing and the screen reads as a status dashboard rather than a generator. Board-size/initial-layout controls are only implied by read-only-looking chips (Grid 8×8, Tiles 64, Seed 1234) with no affordance, and the actual '01 Board & Layout' and '02 Validation' panels sit below the fold, so the promised compact validation feedback is invisible while the user edits rules. Clarity & Hierarchy: The numbered system (03 top-right, 01/02 bottom-left) contradicts reading order, forcing the eye to jump 03 → 01 → 02; the preview frame contains a large dead dark region to the right of the grid, undercutting the 'large focal board' claim and orphaning the P1–P4 legend in a corner. The 'All / Fold' control in the Rule Editor is ambiguous. Visual System & Craft: The page relies on vertical scroll, clipping the Victory Condition card and the 01/02 panel headers at the viewport edge — a jank risk for a 'single main screen' brief. The right rail's six near-identical cards (icon + title + toggle + slider) are repetitive, and the board grid is left-aligned and undersized within its frame, wasting the focal area. Expressiveness: The parchment/gold/serif tabletop identity is genuinely distinctive (dashed inner frame, token orbit dots, category tags like INFO HIDE / DAMAGE), but the rule cards themselves are generic, and the empty board region is a wasted expressive surface. Real trade-off: fitting six rule cards plus layout controls plus validation on one screen conflicts with keeping the board large; the resolution is a fixed-viewport app shell with an internally scrolling rule rail, not a tall scrolling page — prominence of CTAs is bought by moving them to the persistent header rather than a bottom bar that would steal board height.
history.suggestion: Prioritized plan (all CSS/JS-only, offline-safe): 1) Restore the missing CTAs first — add a persistent action cluster in the top-right header: 'Generate Board' as the dominant gold button and 'Start Game' as a secondary outline button, grouped with Export; wire Generate to a brief CSS tile-deal/stagger animation on the grid for a memorable forge moment. 2) Convert the layout to a 100vh app shell with no page scroll: left column = preview (flex-grow) over a compact side-by-side row of '01 Board & Layout' and '02 Validation'; right column = '03 Rule Editor' with internal scroll and a bottom fade mask so no card clips. 3) Turn the chips into real controls inside Board & Layout: a grid-size stepper (6–12), a seed field with a dice reroll icon, and an initial-layout segmented control (Random / Symmetric / Rivers); keep the top chips as live read-only mirrors of those values. 4) Fix preview composition: scale and center the grid to fill ~80% of the frame height, move the P1–P4 legend to a slim vertical strip on the frame's right edge, and use the freed space for 2–3 live validation chips (✓/⚠ color-coded, e.g., '4 players balanced', 'fog leaves 12% unexplored') so feedback is visible while toggling rules. 5) Reorder to match reading flow — 01 Board & Layout → 02 Validation → 03 Rule Editor — keeping the numbered badge system. 6) Tighten the rule rail: consistent card min-heights, relabel 'All / Fold' as 'Collapse all', add hover/focus states, and give each mechanic a distinct glyph treatment so the six cards stop reading as one repeated template.
